content:
Anya K: Customer reports intermittent 504s hitting /v1/generate when they upload large multipart payloads. Started ~09:10 UTC, affecting ~10% of requests. Trace IDs: trace=abc123:gw:504:1, trace=abc123:gw:504:2
Raj P: Which gateway are they hitting? region/us-west-2 or EU?
Anya K: us-west-2 hosted API (prod). They say it repros more when payloads include a 12MB file in the request metadata.
Tomas (oncall): Looks like h2 conn pool churn maybe. Can we get an envoy proxy log for one of those trace IDs?
Anya K: I pulled a sample from ingress logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] trace=abc123 upstream_response_time=8.45s response_code=504 envoy: h2 stream reset: RST_STREAM
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] trace=abc123 listener=ingress-frontend upstream_host=10.2.5.12:443 request_length=12456
```
Support L2: Interesting — upstream took ~8s then got reset. Any 502s mixed in?
Anya K: Yes, small fraction 502s with logs like: `upstream_reset_reason=connection failure` on same time window.
Raj P: Could be backend GC/slow fanning under large request bodies causing SD connection exhaustion. Also billing header mutations were seen in other incidents. Do we have x-billing-* headers present?
Anya K: Customer headers attached: `X-Billing-Account: acct-73`, `X-Rate-Weight: 42`, plus `X-User-Meta` with base64 ~8MB blob.
Tomas (oncall): Whoa — header >8MB is a red flag. Envoy's total header size / buffer could be exceeded and lead to resets. For h2, large headers increase HPACK pressure and can trigger stream resets.
Support L2: Can you reproduce with curl+http2? Try a simple POST with a large custom header to the prod edge (test token) to confirm.
Anya K: Repro steps I ran locally (snipped):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" -H "X-User-Meta: <8MB-base64>" -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Result: 504 after ~8s. No consistent 200.
Tomas (oncall): Ok that suggests header-induced h2 issues. Quick mitigation: we can apply request header size deny at the edge so those requests get a 4xx and don't consume upstream capacity. Can engineering patch a fast-fail rule?
Raj P: Agree. Also for immediate relief, we can route this customer's calls to dedicated fallback route that strips oversized headers (policy-based routing). Ops: can we add a temporary Envoy filter to reject >32KB header blocks?
Support L2: Ops bot — can we create an emergency rule to drop requests with headers >32KB for prod-us-west-2?
ops-bot: Created ticket OPS-3421; applied edge filter in staging. Will roll to prod gated behind canary 1% in 2m.
Tomas (oncall): While canary runs, add a temporary rate limit for this customer to reduce burst. Also capture full access logs for failed requests for root cause conversation with customer.
Anya K: DM'd customer asking for smaller X-User-Meta usage. They said it's generated by an SDK that inlines attachments. They can change client but want us to mitigate now.
Raj P: Longer-term: validate/normalize header size at proxy + recommend moving large binary payloads into body or S3 links. Also add a circuit-breaker for backend connection pool when h2 resets spike.
Support L2: Notes to engineering: Potential fixes: 1) fast-fail oversized headers at edge (4xx) 2) bump envoy per-stream header buffer? risky. 3) strip/limit custom headers per route 4) fallback routing to dedicated pool that accepts larger header frames (if safe).
Tomas (oncall): For immediate postmortem, capture: timeline, customer payload characteristics, envoy reset reasons (RST_STREAM vs PROTOCOL_ERROR), and upstream pod metrics (conn_count, accept queue).
Anya K: Adding logs from upstream svc: 
```
upstream svc-encoder pod-12: accept_queue=48 conn_count=192 mem=2.1GB cpu=55%
prior to event: conn_count peaked 512 and accept_queue==300
```
Support L2: That accept_queue spike matches ephemeral overload. If envoy holds open h2 streams waiting for backend, and headers are huge, it will tie up memory and then RST.
Raj P: Action items:
- Ops: rollback canary if we see bleed-through >0.5% error delta.
- Ops: Ramp up header fast-fail to 100% in 15m if canary healthy.
- Eng (runtime): Add route-level header-size guard and strip policy — P0 for next patch.
- Support: Notify customer of mitigations + ask to switch to body uploads or signed URLs.
Anya K: I'll update the support ticket and schedule a follow-up with the customer in 30m.
Tomas (oncall): Also filing incident report. Tagging: eng-runtime, eng-sre, support.
Support L2: Marking thread resolved once canary hits prod and customer acknowledges workaround. :white_check_mark:
